label: Free 2.0
title: Release communication, not just a changelog
lede: Derivative 2.0 turns the MIT widget from a list of changes into a way to talk to your readers: a richer feed, a modal and banner for the releases that matter, audiences, translations and hints in your product.

items.title: Feed format 2 with media, links and importance
items.text: Mark a release as major and give it a title, a summary, an image and a call to action. The build writes it into changelog.json, the Atom feed and the HTML page.

items.title: Highlight as toast, banner or modal
items.text: One attribute announces the newest unread release with a title, once per reader. Major releases win over newer minor ones, and the modal shows the image and links. This replaces announce from 1.x.

items.title: Audiences, translations and hints
items.text: Show entries only to the readers they matter to, serve titles and entry texts in the reader's language, and let the widget mark the page element an entry is about with data-derivative-hint. Set audience="pro" and hints on the widget.
items.codeTitle: Node script using parseFeed and localizeRelease

items.title: Old widgets keep working
items.text: Format 2 is a superset of format 1, and 1.x feeds are still read. If pages with an old widget cache your feed, keep writing the old format for a while.

items.title: Linear, Jira and Notion as sources (beta)
items.text: Read what shipped straight from a tracker, read-only, with an API token that you keep in the environment. The readers are tested against fixtures of the documented API responses, not against live accounts yet.

note: Upgrading from 1.x? Rename announce to highlight and use Node.js 22 or newer. The migration guide lists every change.
